strategy.note: basis: Tab. 11.20 'Unit process raw data of the cultivation of sweet sorghum' [CN], column 'sweet sorghum', per 1 HECTARE, which yields 4.83E+4 kg of stem and 3.87E+3 kg of grain; the allocation factors of Tab. 11.19 are applied through the per-item factor.; allocation: Physical/economic allocation between sweet sorghum grains and stems per Tab. 11.19: 42.7 % / 57.3 % for fertilisers, pesticides, machinery, transports, land use and all emissions; 20.4 % / 79.6 % for biogenic CO2 and 20.1 % / 79.9 % for the biomass energy.. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

gaps_reported_by_model: The table is per hectare and covers BOTH co-products; every amount here is the per-hectare figure multiplied by the stem allocation share of Tab. 11.19 (57.3 % for fertilisers, pesticides, machinery, transports, land use and all emissions; 79.6 % for the CO2 uptake and 79.9 % for the biomass energy) and then divided by the 48'300 kg of stem per hectare.
No seed input appears in the table.
No water resource for the irrigation is booked directly; only the 'irrigating' service (1.25 ha) is.
The heavy-metal soil emissions are negative (net removal by the crop), which some databases cannot represent.
skipped_items: sweet sorghum stem, at farm: product — reference product of this column, 48'300 kg of stem per hectare. Allocated 100.0 % to the stem per Tab. 11.19.
sweet sorghum grains, at farm: co-product — co-product, 3'870 kg of grain per hectare. Allocated 100.0 % to the stem per Tab. 11.19.
Carbon dioxide, in air: no flow chosen (The keyword search returned no candidate for the CO2 uptake from air, so nothing can be chosen; the line is reported as missing.)

[sulfonyl]urea-compounds, at regional storehouse: no dataset chosen (Neither candidate is the sulfonylurea family: they are nitro- and nitrile-compounds, chemically different pesticide groups. The line is reported as missing.)
transport, tractor and trailer: no dataset chosen (The keyword search returned no candidate for tractor-and-trailer transport, so nothing can be chosen.)
Dinitrogen monoxide: no flow chosen (None of the candidates is dinitrogen monoxide (N2O): they are carbon monoxide variants. Mapping N2O to CO would be a different substance.)
2,4-D: no flow chosen (The keyword search returned no candidate for 2,4-D as a soil emission, so nothing can be chosen.)
